answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake: each agent must lock a small deposit before it can trade, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Like grains of sand building a dune, many small stakes add up to a wall no cheap attacker can climb. A cipher-bound identity check ties each stake to one verifiable key, and the stake is slashed on misbehaviour — an ivory-tower rule with no penalty would fail, because honesty must stay cheaper than fraud.
